messages.phase03.description.1:
Headlamp is the Kubernetes SIG UI web/desktop console for browsing and managing
cluster resources under Kubernetes RBAC. This installs the in-cluster server
with the built-in `view` role for read-only access by default; it does not grant
cluster-admin or expose the UI publicly.
Install Headlamp first when you want the console to browse add-ons installed
later; the installer then discovers their served CRDs and grants get/list/watch.
The Service remains ClusterIP. Use kubectl port-forward, or configure an
independently authenticated Ingress/Gateway after the external entry is ready.
Config: optional Helm values. User values may replace the default RBAC role.
Chart: https://kubernetes-sigs.github.io/headlamp/
messages.phase03.description.2:
Metrics Server exposes recent node and Pod CPU/memory usage through metrics.k8s.io.
It supports kubectl top and resource-based HPA. It is not a monitoring database.
The API server must reach its Service, and Metrics Server must reach each kubelet.
Config: replica count, kubelet TLS choice, and optional Helm values. Keep kubelet
TLS verification enabled unless this is a test cluster with self-signed certs.
messages.phase03.description.3:
cert-manager requests, stores, and renews TLS certificates for Kubernetes apps.
This installs its controllers, webhook, and CRDs. Certificate issuance also
requires an Issuer or ClusterIssuer, which is specific to your CA/DNS provider.
Config: optional Helm values. No public CA credentials are assumed.
messages.phase03.description.4:
kube-prometheus-stack installs Prometheus, Alertmanager, Grafana, exporters,
dashboards, and alert rules. It needs a retention and storage decision.
Config: retention, optional StorageClass/PVC sizes, Grafana admin password,
and optional extra Helm values. Without a StorageClass, metrics are ephemeral.
messages.phase03.description.5:
Loki stores searchable logs; Alloy collects and forwards Kubernetes logs.
Production Loki needs an object-storage design. This installer requires two
user-provided values files: one for Loki storage/deployment and one for Alloy's
collection pipeline and Loki endpoint. It will not use deprecated loki-stack.
Loki: https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/setup/install/helm/
Alloy: https://grafana.com/docs/alloy/latest/configure/kubernetes/
messages.phase03.description.6:
Argo CD reconciles Kubernetes applications from Git or Helm sources.
The chart installs the controller and UI as internal ClusterIP Services.
You must configure repositories, RBAC, and external access for your organization.
Config: optional Helm values; no Git credentials are requested here.
messages.phase03.description.7:
External Secrets Operator copies secret values from a supported external
secret manager into Kubernetes Secrets. This installs the operator only.
Create a SecretStore/ClusterSecretStore and credentials for your provider later.
Config: optional Helm values. No provider is silently chosen.
messages.phase03.description.8:
ExternalDNS manages DNS records from Kubernetes Services and Ingresses.
Gateway HTTPRoutes can be included when Gateway API CRDs are installed.
It requires a DNS provider, domain boundary, ownership ID, and provider auth.
Config: provider, domain, owner ID, optional HTTPRoute source, and a required values file for credentials
or workload identity. Policy defaults to upsert-only (no automatic deletions).
Chart values: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/external-dns/tree/master/charts/external-dns
messages.phase03.description.9:
Velero backs up Kubernetes resources and, with a suitable volume mechanism,
persistent-volume data. It does not replace scheduled etcd snapshots.
Config: a required provider-specific values file for backup storage location,
bucket, credentials/identity, and provider plugin. No object store is assumed.
Chart values: https://github.com/vmware-tanzu/helm-charts/tree/main/charts/velero
messages.phase03.description.10:
NFS CSI dynamically provisions PVCs as directories on an existing NFS export.
The NFS server must already exist and be reachable from every Kubernetes node.
Config: server, exported path, StorageClass name, and reclaim policy.
It will not make this the cluster's default StorageClass automatically.
messages.phase03.description.11:
Envoy Gateway implements Gateway API for application HTTP/TCP routing.
Its Helm chart installs Gateway API CRDs on a new installation. You still need
to create application routes and arrange a LoadBalancer or other external access.
After the controller is ready, this installer can optionally create a basic
HTTP Gateway/HTTPRoute to an existing Service. It does not configure TLS, DNS,
authentication, or a public address.
This is separate from the lb1/lb2 VIP used by the Kubernetes API.
Config: chart version and optional Helm values. Existing foreign Gateway API
CRDs require a separate compatibility review and are not overwritten here.
messages.phase03.description.12:
Kyverno validates, mutates, and generates resources through Kubernetes policies.
Installing its controllers does not enable a policy set. Start with audit/warn
policies, then choose enforcement rules for your own workloads.
Config: optional Helm values.
messages.phase03.description.13:
MetalLB assigns external IPs to LoadBalancer Services on bare metal or Proxmox.
This option configures Layer 2 advertisement and needs a dedicated address range
on the local network. The range must exclude node IPs and the Kubernetes API VIP.
It is generally unsuitable for cloud VPCs; use the cloud load balancer there.
Config: IPv4 address range, pool name, and optional Helm values.
messages.phase03.description.14:
KEDA scales Deployments and Jobs from event sources such as queues or metrics.
It installs the operator and CRDs; each workload still needs a ScaledObject or
ScaledJob and, if required, event-source authentication.
Config: optional Helm values.
messages.phase03.description.15:
Traefik is a maintained controller for standard Kubernetes Ingress resources.
Use spec.ingressClassName: traefik in each application Ingress. The chart also
supports Gateway API separately, but this option enables the Ingress provider.
Community ingress-nginx was retired in March 2026; Traefik is not a drop-in
replacement for its annotations or behavior. Review existing routes before migration.
Config: controller replicas, Service type, and optional Helm values. NodePort
needs network access to the assigned ports; LoadBalancer needs a working provider
such as MetalLB or a cloud load balancer. This does not reuse the Kubernetes API VIP.
messages.phase03.description.16:
Longhorn provides replicated block volumes and a storage UI using disks/filesystems
on Kubernetes nodes. It is useful when no external SAN/NAS is available; it is not
a substitute for off-cluster backups or an independent failure domain.
Every storage node must meet the upstream host requirements, including open-iscsi
and a running iscsid service for the default V1 engine, plus supported host
utilities. Before installation, the installer uses the phase-2 SSH mesh to
install and enable these dependencies on every Kubernetes node automatically.
It avoids the incompatible open-iscsi 2.1.12 release. Mount propagation is only
needed for Longhorn Base Image. Dedicated data disks are optional, but the
selected/default data path must have sufficient capacity on eligible nodes.
Config: replica count, optional default-StorageClass choice, and optional values.
No disk is formatted and no data path is changed by this installer.
Longhorn's own snapshots are available after installation; Kubernetes generic
VolumeSnapshot APIs require the separate external-snapshotter controller, which
this menu does not install.
Chart: https://charts.longhorn.io
messages.phase03.source.selection_help:
1) Official (default) - each add-on's upstream chart and image registries
 2) DaoCloud (China)   - file proxy + multi-registry OCI/image proxy
 3) 1Panel (China)     - Docker Hub via 1Panel; files/other public registries via DaoCloud
 4) Google (global)    - popular Docker Hub image cache; other downloads stay upstream
 5) Custom enterprise - Harbor/ACR/TCR etc.; requires registry-path mapping and file proxy
 0) Keep current selection and continue
Public mirrors may rate-limit, miss artifacts or be unreachable. Google may miss OCI charts.
HTTPS and certificate validation stay enabled. Unknown private registries stay unchanged.
messages.phase03.menu.body:
1) Headlamp              - Kubernetes visual cluster console (recommended first)
 2) Metrics Server        - CPU/memory API for kubectl top and HPA
 3) cert-manager          - issue and renew application TLS certificates
 4) Prometheus stack      - metrics, alerts, dashboards, and Grafana
 5) Loki + Alloy          - centralized log storage and collection
 6) Argo CD               - GitOps application delivery
 7) External Secrets      - sync secrets from an external secret manager
 8) ExternalDNS           - synchronize Service/Ingress/HTTPRoute DNS
 9) Velero                - Kubernetes resource and volume backups
10) NFS CSI               - dynamic PVCs from an existing NFS server
11) Envoy Gateway         - Gateway API application traffic controller
12) Kyverno               - Kubernetes policy engine
13) MetalLB               - bare-metal LoadBalancer IPs (Layer 2)
14) KEDA                  - event-driven workload autoscaling
15) Traefik Ingress       - controller for standard Kubernetes Ingress
16) Longhorn              - distributed block storage from node disks
 S) Download source       - choose chart/image sources for all add-ons
 L) Language              - switch English / Chinese
 0) Exit
=========================================================

messages.ops.cli.stats_cidr: Stats management CIDR; empty string restricts to loopback
messages.ops.host.command: Host command failed: %s; raw output is kept private.
messages.ops.host.failed: The host action failed. Inspect the private host journal.
messages.ops.host.inactive: The required host service is not active; no change was made.
messages.ops.host.layout: The host configuration is not a supported toolkit-managed layout.
messages.ops.host.rollback: Automatic rollback failed; retain the lock and inspect the host backup.
messages.ops.host.uncertain: The remote outcome is uncertain. Do not clear the lock until the remote job has stopped.
messages.ops.lifecycle.inventory: The declared Kubernetes node inventory does not match the cluster.
messages.ops.lifecycle.local_data: Local or temporary workload data prevents safe drain. Review storage and explicit data-removal intent.
messages.ops.lifecycle.not_ready: The node is not Ready; it cannot return to scheduling.
messages.ops.lifecycle.quorum: There are not enough healthy control planes for this maintenance action.
messages.ops.lifecycle.scheduling: The node scheduling state did not reach the expected result.
messages.ops.restore.completed: Verified data restored into isolated directory: %s
messages.ops.restore.report_failed: Isolated recovery completed, but its report could not be saved. Inspect restore.json before retrying.
messages.ops.restore.serving_unverified: Data was restored offline; service startup and Kubernetes recovery have not been verified by this command.
messages.ops.restore.source: Backup source identity does not match the explicitly expected fingerprint.
messages.ops.restore.version: Recovery requires the recorded, matching etcdutl version and a valid revision increment.
messages.common.package.wait_lock: Waiting for the current package-manager operation to finish; lock files and processes are preserved.
messages.common.package.lock_timeout: Package-manager lock wait failed or timed out. Retry after the running task completes.
messages.common.package.invalid_timeout: Package lock timeout must be an integer in 1..3600 seconds.
messages.phase01.error.package_runtime_missing: Package coordination runtime is missing; copy the complete source package.
messages.ops.change.report_failed: The operation completed, but its report could not be saved. Check the cluster journal before retrying.
messages.ops.change.plan_report_failed: The plan file was saved, but its report could not be saved. Inspect the plan path before retrying.
messages.phase02.config.enrollment_required: Register SSH access for the configured nodes before noninteractive deployment.
messages.phase02.config.enrollment_retry: Pairing failed. Verify the target node and its current pairing code, then retry.
messages.ops.cli.retained_user: Independent SSH account that retains administration after bootstrap removal
messages.ops.security.separate_identity: Use a different non-root administration account for the handoff.
messages.ops.security.account_missing: The retained administration account does not exist on a registered node.
messages.ops.security.foreign_grant: Bootstrap sudoers content differs from the toolkit-owned grant; review it before removal.
messages.ops.security.probe_failed: Independent SSH and sudo verification failed; review the node's rollback journal before retrying.
messages.ops.security.control_identity: Connect the API coordinator through the retained administration account before finalizing access.
messages.ops.cli.diagnostics: Collect a private, allowlisted cluster diagnostic bundle
messages.ops.diagnostics.unverified: API view unavailable or exceeds limits: %s
messages.ops.diagnostics.review: Review internal names and addresses before sharing. Credentials, logs and free-form event messages are excluded.
messages.ops.operation.security_finalize: Hand off administration and remove bootstrap access
messages.ops.maintenance.uncordon: Return a Ready node to scheduling
messages.ops.security.handoff_guide: First provision an independent administration account with SSH and sudo access on every registered node. The API coordinator must use that retained account.
messages.ops.lock.recovery_guide: Stop the previous coordinator and its remote jobs first. Recovery requires the current owner, resourceVersion and the exact confirmation: OLD COORDINATOR AND REMOTE JOBS STOPPED
messages.ops.cli.to_version: Target Kubernetes patch version, for example v1.36.6
messages.ops.upgrade.version: Only a newer patch in the current minor is supported; all actual versions must match the planned source or target.
messages.ops.upgrade.package: An exact target package is unavailable or installed package verification failed. Refresh approved package metadata before planning.
messages.phase01.message.machine_id: Preparing a unique machine-id before the first reboot
messages.phase01.error.identity_generation: Fresh-node identity preparation failed; an existing Kubernetes node will not be reidentified. Copy the complete package and inspect permissions.
messages.ops.cli.data_device: Prepared storage policy: none or existing; enrollment never formats a new disk
messages.ops.lifecycle.join_storage: Worker enrollment accepts only prepared none/existing storage layouts. Prepare disks through phase one first.
messages.ops.lifecycle.join_state: Node enrollment state is inconsistent. Inspect existing Kubernetes state before generating a fresh continuation plan.
messages.ops.lifecycle.duplicate_identity: The new node's machine-id is missing or duplicates a registered node. Prepare a fresh clone before enrollment.
messages.ops.backup.tools: Matching etcd tools could not be verified from the local container image. Inspect its digest, platform, available disk space and tool cache; no snapshot was published.
messages.ops.cli.restore_rehearse: Restore into a new directory, verify etcd over loopback mTLS, then stop it
messages.ops.restore.rehearsed: Isolated etcd served the restored cluster identity over mTLS and was stopped.
messages.ops.restore.rehearsal_scope: This rehearsal requires a verified control-plane backup and a fresh isolated restore.
messages.ops.restore.cluster_identity: The source cluster identity is missing or does not match the isolated data. Take a fresh backup with cluster identity metadata.
messages.ops.restore.ports: Loopback ports 12379/12380 are occupied; no existing listener was changed. Use an isolated rehearsal host.
messages.ops.restore.rehearsal_failed: Isolated etcd verification failed; inspect the private rehearsal log. The live etcd service was not targeted.
messages.ops.lifecycle.pdb: A matching PDB has no safe eviction budget, stale status, or overlaps another PDB. Review its policy and healthy replicas before retrying.
messages.ops.lifecycle.workloads: Workload controllers have not recovered their expected Ready replicas. The serial operation stopped before advancing to another node.
messages.phase02.error.existing_cluster_plan: Existing Kubernetes state was found, but this coordinator has no saved deployment plan. Restore the original plan to resume; use 06 for ongoing cluster operations.
messages.ops.dns.layout: The CoreDNS scheduling layout is invalid or did not match after restoration. Review its deployment UID and scheduling policy.
messages.ops.cli.change_continue: Build a new confirmed plan from failed intent and current facts; keep the old plan as history
messages.ops.change.lock_namespace: All operations for a cluster must use the kube-system lock namespace.
messages.ops.change.recovered: The stopped coordinator was explicitly recovered; generate and confirm a new continuation plan.
messages.ops.upgrade.maintenance_owner: A node is already paused by an administrator or another operation. Restore it explicitly or continue its verified failed upgrade plan.
messages.phase02.progress.verify_existing: The completed deployment matches its saved intent; verifying the existing cluster without reinstalling services.
messages.phase02.error.etcd_layout: The expected etcd Pods are not all Running and Ready.
messages.phase02.error.service_route: %s has no route to Service address %s. Configure an internal default gateway or an explicit Service-CIDR route before deployment; Internet access is not required.
messages.phase02.error.dns_layout: CoreDNS Pods must be Ready and placed separately across all control-plane nodes.
messages.ops.host.reserved: An unfinished LB transaction reserves this host. Stop its coordinator and jobs, then inspect and recover it from menu 6 in 05.
messages.lb.transaction.none: No interrupted LB reservation was found.
messages.lb.transaction.guide: Confirm the old coordinator and remote jobs have stopped. rollback restores the saved configuration; finish retains the committed configuration. Changed files cause recovery to stop.
messages.lb.transaction.confirm: Type STOPPED LB COORDINATOR AND JOBS
messages.lb.transaction.recovered: The selected LB transactions were recovered.
messages.ops.cli.replacement_name: New, distinct worker hostname for replacement
messages.ops.operation.node_replace: Replace a worker with a prepared new identity
messages.ops.lifecycle.retire_state: Worker retirement could not be proven safe. Check the pinned identity, static Pods, remaining sandboxes and retirement record; disks were not reset.
messages.ops.lifecycle.storage_evacuation: Node-bound storage has not been evacuated or CSI attachments remain. Evacuate replicas and detach volumes before withdrawing this worker.
messages.ops.cli.materials_prepare: Build locked delivery material on a connected reference control-plane host
messages.ops.cli.materials_verify: Verify a delivery directory and every artifact without installing
messages.ops.cli.materials_import: Activate verified offline material on this prepared Ubuntu host
messages.ops.cli.materials: Absolute path to the delivery directory
messages.ops.cli.material_id: Expected material ID from a trusted delivery channel
messages.ops.materials.invalid: Invalid material lock, platform metadata or artifact layout.
messages.ops.materials.incomplete: Required packages, images, tools or chart material are missing.
messages.ops.materials.platform: This action requires root on Ubuntu 24.04 amd64. Verification can run on other supported management hosts.
messages.ops.materials.download: A required HTTPS artifact could not be downloaded. No complete material was published.
messages.ops.materials.os_upgrade: Offline mode installs the locked deployment dependencies. Full operating-system patching requires a separately maintained offline OS repository.
messages.ops.preview.stats: HAProxy stats allowed source: %s; update registered LBs and publish the configuration.
messages.ops.preview.security: Remove toolkit deployment grants for %s after proving independent management as %s on: %s.
messages.ops.preview.upgrade: Kubernetes %s → %s; serial nodes: %s. Preserve CoreDNS scheduling and verify each rollout.
messages.ops.preview.join: Join prepared worker %s (%s) with a temporary credential; preserve existing storage.
messages.ops.preview.retire: Withdraw worker %s (UID %s): evict, stop kubelet and known daemon sandboxes, remove Node; preserve disks and configuration.
messages.ops.preview.replace: Withdraw %s, then join distinct worker %s (%s); stop and replan on partial failure.
messages.ops.cli.ca_file: Public CA PEM file; omit to use system trust
messages.ops.operation.registry_configure: Configure HTTPS trust for an enterprise registry
messages.ops.preview.registry: Configure HTTPS registry %s with CA fingerprint %s on Kubernetes nodes; no insecure TLS fallback or system-wide CA change.
messages.ops.registry.certificate: The public CA certificate or its pinned fingerprint is invalid.
messages.ops.registry.endpoint: Registry HTTPS identity or /v2/ connectivity could not be verified from this node.
messages.ops.config.operations_only: This configuration includes ongoing operations settings. Use the base configuration for initial 02 deployment, then apply registry trust through 06.
messages.phase01.message.offline_dns: Verified offline material is active; public repository DNS is not required. Node addressing and SSH are still checked.
messages.phase01.error.network_check: Network readiness check failed; inspect the preceding DNS or offline-material error.
messages.ops.cli.chart: Trusted Cilium chart archive; its bytes and version are pinned in the plan
messages.ops.operation.component_upgrade: Upgrade Cilium by a controlled same-minor patch rollout
messages.ops.preview.component: Target Cilium %s; chart SHA-256 %s. Freeze automatic agent/envoy replacement, evict one node at a time under PDB, verify health, then restore rollout policy.
messages.ops.component.chart: The Cilium chart is missing, malformed, too large or has a different name/version.
messages.ops.component.version: Only stable Cilium 1.20 patch upgrades on Kubernetes 1.33–1.36 are supported by this adapter. Downgrades and minor jumps are refused.
messages.ops.component.policy: The component topology, rollout policy or owned resources do not match the supported layout.
messages.ops.component.image_override: Existing Helm image overrides do not resolve to the requested Cilium version. Review the values before creating a plan.
messages.ops.component.release: The Helm release state does not match this plan. Inspect pending operations and the previous coordinator; force rollback is not automatic.
messages.ops.component.not_ready: The controlled Cilium rollout has not recovered its expected Pod/node health; it stopped before advancing.
messages.ops.cli.evidence_file: Private JSON declaration of an external encrypted backup
messages.ops.cli.protection_status: Inspect PVC/application protection declarations and restore gaps
messages.ops.preview.protection: Register %s declared objects, ciphertext SHA-256 %s. Checks bytes and object identities; decryption and application restore remain unverified.
messages.ops.protection.invalid: Invalid protection declaration; check schema, cluster identity, timestamp, object UIDs and artifact metadata.
messages.ops.protection.private_file: Protection evidence must be an owned regular file with private permissions and no symbolic links.
messages.ops.protection.ciphertext: The artifact lacks the supported age ciphertext header; no plaintext data is registered.
messages.ops.protection.identity: A declared protection object is absent or its UID changed; regenerate the declaration.
messages.ops.protection.record: The immutable protection record is invalid or belongs to another owner/cluster.
messages.ops.protection.summary: Protection inventory: %s objects; %s unregistered; %s stale identities. Registration is not decryption or restore proof.
messages.ops.protection.state.identity-stale: Object missing or rebuilt; old evidence does not cover its current identity
messages.ops.protection.state.unregistered: No declaration; backup and restore are unverified
messages.ops.protection.state.registered-restore-: Declared and ciphertext checked at registration; decryption and restore unverified
messages.ops.materials.apt_security: The material builder requires authenticated APT sources and HTTPS certificate verification. Remove trusted=yes and insecure transport overrides before preparing a signed closure.
messages.ops.protection.state.superseded-identity: Old identity retained as history; a declaration matches the current object UID
messages.ops.native.outcome: Entry %s / %s: %s; failures %s; skipped %s. This summarizes the selected native action only.
messages.ops.native.report_failed: The native action may have completed, but its report could not be saved. Inspect the action result before repeating any change.
messages.ops.containerd.invalid: Unsupported or conflicting containerd sandbox configuration; no unsafe rewrite was applied.
messages.ops.containerd.drift: CRI sandbox image differs from the Kubernetes target.
messages.ops.containerd.failed: Sandbox-image preparation failed; inspect the private configuration backup and containerd service before continuing.
